_: The storyteller's pace (director.js; Left 4 Dead's director, CK3's pushback). tension: 0 calm to 1 the realm on fire (wars between the houses, towns rioting or starving, a usurper, the threat itself), kept as the reign's curve. After quietByAct seasons since the King's last crisis (whatever the houses do among themselves; the first about 80 s in, under a minute apart in the last act, at 40 s a season; Mac 2026-11-17: 'no war in 2-3 minutes' when it was 4 seasons of 80 s), one threat rises at a place and grows by its grow each season until the King answers it there (an order in answers, at one of its towns) or it breaks at 1. After any crisis (a threat that passes or breaks, a house that rises), breather seasons of rest, and no house rises meanwhile (tension in waves). quietByAct: those seasons by act of the reign, so threats come sooner as it builds (Mac 2026-11-16: 'tension in short intervals, highs and lows'; was 9,9,6,3 with a breather of 6, about five minutes between threats). finale: in the last act there is no breather; finale.kind: the threat the house the last act names raises (reign.js names the coldest house and the season it lands, gameplay review #8); a named story or pretender is the climax and the director stays out of its way; when no such threat is named, one threat rises at once and grows to land at landAt of the reign's clock. says: what the realm reports as it grows (by level), {house} {town} {n}; answers: the orders that answer it at its place (a host is met with men or an oath, never bought off with a gift or a feast; Mac 2026-11-17: war is the crux; the first is the one the Hand offers first), each in proportion (no cheap gesture dissolves a threat): ends ends it; delay buys that many seasons (bigDelay against a host of 6 companies or more), and the lord remembers it; ease takes that much off it, and it ends only if that brings it to nothing before it lands; anywhere: given at Kingsmere (the banners, the levy), not at the place; toHouse: given to the threat's house (a grant), wherever the town. pushback: a King too comfortable (peace, purse in gold, the houses' mean favour all at or over these) draws envy every few seasons: the strongest other house cools by envy and a threat comes sooner.

finale._grace: reign.js tick: the reign's clock waits while the climax the last act named is still coming (the pretender's rumour or march, the finale's host, the named story running), at most grace of the reign's length past its hour; Thronefall's last night is fought, not timed out (the Last Accord, 2026-11-16: Thornvale's host named at turn 55 was still on the road when the clock ended the reign at 63).

says: {house}'s host at {town} grows: {n} companies under arms
{house}'s host at {town} is ready to march
host.broke: {house}'s host marches out of {town}, against the crown's towns
host.why: An army does not gather for nothing. Meet it with spears, or make them allies, or it marches from {town}.

banners.label: Call the banners to match their host

march.label: Break the host before it marches

levy.label: Raise the royal levy to match their host

says: {town} is starving, and the hunger reaches its neighbours
famine.passed: The King's grain reaches {town}, and the hunger eases
famine.why: A hungry town shrinks, riots and blames its King. Grain now costs less than a rising later.

relief.label: Send grain from the royal stores

says: Banners that are not the King's are seen at {town}
At {town}, {house} speaks of a better claim to the throne
pretender.broke: {house} proclaims a pretender at {town}; every house is asked to choose
pretender.passed: The pretender's banners at {town} come down
pretender.why: A claim left unanswered gathers friends. Bind {house} to the crown, or shame them.

grant.label: Grant them land to quiet the claim

marriage.label: Wed the claim into the crown's line

ward.label: Take their heir as a royal ward

march.label: Put down the claim by force
